claims.text: The investigated CrFeCoNiX alloys are synthesized as single-phase solid solutions.
Increasing the effective concentration of Si, Mn, or Al promotes preferential segregation of that element to the metal–oxide interface during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential segregation of X leads to formation of a compositionally graded mixed Cr–X oxide.
The mixed Cr–X oxide minimizes defects at the metal–oxide interface.
The mixed Cr–X oxide reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between the scale and substrate.
Reducing interfacial defects and thermal-expansion mismatch produces a coherent, slow-growing protective barrier resistant to cracking and spallation above 900 °C.
The compositionally graded mixed Cr–X oxide has improved lattice matching with the alloy substrate.
During high-temperature oxidation, X migrates to the metal–oxide interface.
At the metal–oxide interface, X oxidizes and mixes with chromium.
The mixed Cr–X oxide anchors the oxide scale.
Alloys with enhanced X segregation will form a continuous, slow-growing oxide layer with minimal cracking or spallation.
Alloys lacking significant X segregation will exhibit rapid oxide formation followed by cracking or spallation.
Control alloys with lower or non-promoted X concentrations are expected to form less stable oxide layers.
APT can provide quantitative profiles of X segregation at the metal–oxide interface.
In-situ XPS can track the evolving oxide chemistry during the proposed experiment.
